headline: Huawei says it has shipped more than 100 million devices with its own Kirin chips since 2023, despite US sanctions, and that its new Kirin 9050 series is in mass production.
score_reason: Pool score kept: the milestone is a company claim that is not independently verified.
importance_line: It suggests Huawei can keep producing its own phone chips under US sanctions, which matters to Chinese consumers and to US export-control policy, but the 100 million figure and the chip claims are Huawei's own, with no independent testing or breakdown reported.
summary: Tech Edition reports that Huawei announced on 13 Oct 2026 that it has shipped more than 100 million Kirin-powered devices since returning to the premium phone market in 2023, without giving a breakdown by model or market. Huawei also described its Kirin 9050 series as the first mass-produced chip built on its LogicFolding design, reporting a 53.5% gain in transistor density, and said it reached mass production "with the support of China's domestic electronics supply chain".
notes: SCMP (the pool item) was blocked; the story was read on Tech Edition, which reports Huawei's own announcement.
